clue.text: Surveyors' means of measuring sports-grounds

definitions.meaning: ... hairs or a ... rod let a surveyor read distance through a telescope
plural of stadium, an arena for games

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a surveying instrument for gauging distance; the other is the plural of an arena for athletics.

clue.text: So insincere, was Janus

definitions.meaning: deceitful, saying one thing and meaning another
the Roman god Janus is pictured with a face looking each way

explanation.surface: Janus, the god with two faces, held up as the emblem of insincerity.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicitous people are said to have two faces, and the Roman god of doorways literally had a pair of them.

clue.text: Skirmish involving 24s may be above our heads

definitions.meaning: 24 across is a breed of terrier, so a skirmish involving them is a scrap between canines
a close aerial battle between fighter planes happens overhead

explanation.surface: A brief clash that might be taking place in the sky overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 24 across, a terrier breed, so the first sense is a scrap among hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap between canines and a close-range air battle between warplanes share the same name.

clue.text: Exciting incident! He's beheaded after coming to Abrahamville

indicators.note: the beheaded word is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
Abraham came from Ur of the Chaldees, so his home town is Ur

indicators.note: the word loses its head, meaning its first letter goes

parts.note: the pronoun he, the 's being 'is'

explanation.surface: A dramatic tale of someone losing his head on arriving in a biblical town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abrahamville' is a whimsical name for UR, the patriarch's birthplace in Genesis; 'beheaded' strips the H from HE, leaving E.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is a thrilling or daring experience, a stirring episode.

clue.text: Current staff protecting sick king

indicators.note: the staff wraps round and shields the other pieces

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff of office
sick means ill
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A rod held protectively over an ailing monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A millrace is the channel of flowing water that drives a mill wheel, so a current or stream.

clue.text: Politician's ruined — first time with no seat

indicators.note: ruined suggests the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A politician's career is wrecked the first time he loses his seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' shuffles the letters of FIRST TIME and NO SEAT together.
explanation.definitionFit: In UK government a junior departmental minister below cabinet rank holds this title.

clue.text: Dictionary of Roman Law — one to pore over

parts.note: lex is the Latin word for law
I is the Roman numeral for one
to con is to study closely

explanation.surface: A glossary of ancient legal terms that a student must study.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a wordbook, the vocabulary of a language set out alphabetically.

clue.text: Defector has a job making tea

parts.note: a post is a position of employment

indicators.note: making signals that the letters of tea are fashioned into something new

explanation.surface: A turncoat who has taken a job as a tea-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate is someone who renounces a faith or cause, a turncoat.

clue.text: Finished embodying alternative strategy originally approved

indicators.note: the first word holds the other pieces within its body

parts.note: finished means ended
or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word strategy

explanation.surface: A plan that has been completed, with another option built in, finally gets the go-ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to sanction or back, so endorsed means given official backing.

clue.text: Let off a few in foreign parts

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the rearranged letters
in foreign parts suggests the word is broken up and its letters scattered

parts.note: as printed; the setter meant a five, V being the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Being pardoned for a few misdeeds committed abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' rearranges FOREIGN; V is placed in it. As printed 'a few' cannot give V, so the clue must have read 'a five'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be let off is to be excused or pardoned an offence.

clue.text: Where one could obtain beef for a penny once?

parts.note: an ox is a beef animal
taken as written
d was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Asking where cattle could once be bought for a single penny.
explanation.walkthrough: D (from Latin denarius) stood for the old British penny before 1971; the answer is the English university city.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue asks for a place, and this English university city is that location.

clue.text: Sounds like a game for those being treated

indicators.note: the clue openly says we want a word that is spoken the same as the game

parts.note: patience is a card game for one player, called solitaire in the US

explanation.surface: A remark that hospital waiting might be a game of endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: The card game PATIENCE (American solitaire) is said the same way as the word for people under medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: People under the care of a doctor or in hospital are the ones receiving medical treatment.

clue.text: Duck a tax once demanded by a king

parts.note: scot was an old tax or levy, as in scot-free
ER, Edwardus Rex, is the royal cipher of King Edward

explanation.surface: A historic levy imposed by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOT survives in 'scot-free', untaxed; ER here is Edward Rex rather than the usual queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck of northern coasts.

clue.text: English poet without a doctor

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the poet's name surrounds the letter

parts.note: A. E. Housman wrote A Shropshire Lad

explanation.surface: A British poet who lacks a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. A houseman is the old British name for a junior hospital doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a junior resident hospital medic was called by this title, like an American intern.

clue.text: Improvement people in the commercial intended to be heard

indicators.note: the people go inside the commercial

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a commercial
men means people

indicators.note: the word for intended is spoken, and we write down what we hear

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like MENT

explanation.surface: A better version of the people in an advert, meant to be listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be heard' gives MENT, which is said like MEANT (intended).
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change made to correct or better something.

clue.text: His lad, I trust, has access to mine

indicators.note: the phrase has, or holds within it, the letters we want

explanation.surface: A father trusts that his son can get into his own property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' tells you the answer is held inside 'lad, I trust'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage leading into a mine from a hillside.

clue.text: A prisoner inside, also a S. American exponent of squeeze

indicators.note: the first pieces sit inside the following ones

parts.note: and means also
taken as written
con is short for convict
taken as written

explanation.surface: A convict inside, who also proves a South American master of the bear hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is the container signal; the surface's convict and squeeze hint at prison, but the definition is the constricting South American snake.
explanation.definitionFit: This huge snake of South American rivers kills its prey by constriction.

clue.text: Of poor quality, like Mercury and Venus?

definitions.meaning: the planets whose orbits lie within the Earth's are termed this by astronomers

explanation.definitionFit: Second-rate goods are lower in quality, and planets orbiting closer to the Sun than Earth bear the same astronomical label.

clue.text: State publicity for liquor

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
an ad gives publicity

explanation.surface: A state advertising campaign for alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic drink brewed from fermented honey.

clue.text: Go round the bend' comprehending northern comic dramatist

indicators.note: comprehending in its sense of including, so the letter is taken inside

parts.note: a river that meanders winds round bend after bend

explanation.surface: A northern comedian driven mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go round the bend' looks like going mad but means winding along. Menander was the Greek writer of New Comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Menander was an ancient Athenian playwright of New Comedy.

clue.text: Redolent of a foreign capital with sound credit

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name for Rome

indicators.note: this word tells us the next piece is spoken, and we spell what we hear

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Smelling of an overseas city with a good credit rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' gives TIC, said like TICK, British slang for credit; 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something redolent gives off a strong fragrance, so it smells spicy and fragrant.

clue.text: One reeks badly after using this fuel

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stinks after handling paraffin.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerosene is paraffin oil, burnt in lamps and jet engines.

clue.text: Which woman identified an American insect?

definitions.meaning: the reply to the question is that a girl named ... it
a large green North American grasshopper named for its call

explanation.surface: A whodunit question about which lady spotted a bug in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A large green bush cricket of North America is named for its rasping song, and the reply naming the woman is the same phrase.

clue.text: Do as an inventor does — kick up a stink

explanation.definitionFit: Inventors bring things into being, while making a fuss is the informal British sense of the same verb.

clue.text: Parts of the body employed in mortal combat?

definitions.text: Parts of the body employed in mortal combat?

parts.words: Parts of the body employed in mortal combat?
parts.note: two body parts, the flanks and the limbs, joined to make the weapons a soldier carries at his belt

explanation.surface: Limbs and torso put to use in a fight to the death.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols or swords worn at the hip are carried at the soldier's flank rather than shouldered.

clue.text: Sad change after Scotsman rejected watery spirits

indicators.note: the rearranged word follows the other piece
rejected suggests the name is sent back the way it came

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of sad are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scotsman, turned down, becomes gloomy about the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns IAN into NAI; 'change' makes ADS from SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiads are water nymphs of Greek myth, living in springs and rivers.

clue.text: Amusing story of wild cat on Dee

indicators.note: wild signals that the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A funny tale of an untamed cat by the River Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges CAT ON DEE; the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short entertaining tale of a real incident.

clue.text: Barker's super Russian beer

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I
red, as Soviet Russia was called
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone shouting the praises of an excellent Russian brew.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (top-notch) is written with the digit read as the letter I; 'Barker' is a dog, not a market trader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier, and dogs are what bark.

clue.text: Not quite the people for Orpheus's country

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls a letter short at its end

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
a race is a people

explanation.surface: Saying the populace were not quite suited to the land of Orpheus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter of THE to give TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpheus, the mythical musician, was said to come from the ancient region north of Greece.
